top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, firm heterogeneity and selection in trade) is a mature, well-defined discovery, over twenty years old. Melitz (2003) is the originating model, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extends it to the exporting-versus-FDI choice. Its central selection and reallocation result has been tested repeatedly on firm-level administrative and customs data from many countries. It is also distinct from the 2008 trade prize, which concerned representative-firm intra-industry trade and location. The main cost is that Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum are not credited on this entry, so the citation should be worded around the theoretical framework. I judge that cost smaller than the attribution problem in P002, where three names must be cut from eight credited contributors, and smaller than the narrower scope and weaker empirical identification of P003. P002 ranks second for its breadth of policy influence and the separability of Calvo, Taylor and Woodford. P003 ranks third as a clean, original two-author mechanism that is distinct from the 2022 prize. All three are worthy of an award, so I rank no award last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. I have no co-authorship or institutional tie to Melitz, Helpman, Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Kiyotaki or Moore. I overlapped institutionally at Stockholm University (2010-17) with committee members Hassler and Krusell, who are not candidates. That overlap is not co-authorship. My 2021 presentation speech as chair does not establish private preferences among the 2026 candidates.
